html:
The Tahltan are an Athabaskan people of the Stikine River country in northwestern British Columbia. Tāłtān Konelīne is their name for their homeland, which centres on Telegraph Creek and Dease Lake.

They hunted caribou, moose and mountain goats and fished salmon. Obsidian from Mount Edziza in their land was traded widely. Coastal Tlingit traders came up the Stikine for furs, and the Tahltan married with them and with the Kaska and Tagish. Gold rushes on the Stikine and in the Cassiar country in the 1860s and 1870s, and the Klondike rush of 1898, brought miners through. In 1910 Tahltan chiefs signed a declaration asserting their rights to their land, and in recent decades they have opposed mining in the headwaters of the Stikine.
